name: fast-http
workload: Parsing the same ~500-byte HTTP GET request header (with several headers) 100,000 times, compared against joyent/http-parser (C) running the equivalent loop
claimed_speedup: fast-http is 1.25x faster than http-parser: 0.086s vs 0.108s to parse the same header 100,000 times
compiler_and_flags: fast-http run under SBCL 1.2.6; http-parser (C) side compiled with unstated compiler/flags
tradeoffs: Common Lisp only (requires SBCL/CL runtime), not directly usable from C++; low-level API avoids allocation during parsing but callback-driven API differs from http-parser's; benchmark uses one fixed payload size rather than a range
caveats: Repo has no separate LICENSE file (MIT is only declared in fast-http.asd's :license field); benchmark ran on Travis CI shared runners with CPU model unstated and no compiler flags given for the C-side comparison, so capped at tier C rather than A/B; only one workload size tested
found_via: Hacker News: query "fast http parser" (tags=story), hit "A fast HTTP request/response parser for Common Lisp" (item 8534866, https://github.com/fukamachi/fast-http)

name: SynapServe
workload: Parsing synthetic HTTP/1.1 requests of three sizes (35B GET/1 header, 368B POST/9 headers, 733B POST/20 headers) and header-lookup latency on a pre-parsed 9-header request, using Criterion with 100 samples on a single core, vs httparse 1.10
claimed_speedup: 1.11-1.15x faster raw parse throughput (1.71 vs 1.49 GiB/s on medium requests; 1.63 vs 1.47 GiB/s on large); 1.38-1.46x faster when including semantic/header extraction that httparse defers to the caller; 32-37x faster header lookup (0.59-0.67ns O(1) vs 20.5-23.1ns O(n) in httparse)
tradeoffs: Claims zero-allocation, io_uring-based server design; the larger 1.38-1.46x figures bundle semantic/header-indexing work that httparse intentionally leaves to the caller, so those comparisons are not strictly apples-to-apples; single-core microbenchmark only
caveats: No public source repository found: the linked GitHub org (github.com/SynapServe) states 'This organization has no public repositories', despite the site claiming an open-source core, so has_code/usability/license could not be confirmed; no CPU model, OS, compiler, or build flags stated for the benchmark; baseline (httparse) is a widely-used incumbent but is not one of the three named assignment baselines (llhttp/http-parser/picohttpparser)
found_via: Hacker News: query "zero-copy http parser" (tags=story), hit "Show HN: SynapServe – zero-allocation HTTP server in Rust with io_uring" (item 47136572, https://synapserve.io)
